get.description: Sets the CSRF cookie and returns the token the client must echo in X-CSRFToken.

post.description:
Sign out. The portal session ends here; the answer carries the form the browser posts to
Keycloak's end-session endpoint, which ends the Keycloak session too (and so every other
application signed in with it, by back-channel logout: the drafting tool's sessions in that
Keycloak session end that way since P25b).

patch.description:
One's own name, time zone and title. The name changes on the records profile too, in the
same transaction (`identity.update_profile`), and on the Keycloak account after it.

get.description:
The person's password date, passkeys, recovery codes and authenticator app, as Keycloak
holds them (labels and dates only; never a secret).

Asked by the sign-in pages (the sclu theme, on the portal's own address), so that the page
where someone sets up their second step offers an authenticator app only while Settings
allows one. Settings' switch, nothing about any person.

To Keycloak's sign-in (a full page load, not a fetch). `next` is where to come back to;
`kc_action` asks Keycloak for one of its own credential pages instead (signed-in people
only); `login_hint` and `expired` (a flag; the hours are Settings') fill in the "signed out
after N hours" page (005); `second_step=app` (P25c) is someone setting up their first second
step who chose an authenticator app on the passkey page, honoured while Settings allows apps
(otherwise the sign-in is the usual one, and its first second step a passkey).

Back from Keycloak. Checked (state, PKCE, nonce, the ID token, the second step), the person
found, then signed in here with a portal session of their own.

post.description:
Keycloak says a session is over (OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout 1.0): the person signed
out in another application, an administrator ended their sessions, or Keycloak ended them.
The portal sessions it names end now. 400 for a token that does not pass the spec's checks.

get.description:
Every person's name, email and role. Anyone on the team (P20h: interns and limited-scope
attorneys hand work to a colleague too); not administrators only. A signed-in requester is
refused with the records API's own 403.

post.description:
Make the account and have Keycloak email the person a link to join: choose a password, add
a passkey, save recovery codes (P15a; P25a). A requester gets the account only: the public
has no sign-in (owner, 2026-10-20).

P25a (205 "Send password reset"): Keycloak emails the person a link to choose a new
password. Signing in afterwards still takes their passkey.

P25a: end every session the person has, in the portal now and in Keycloak (so in every
application signed in through it) as soon as Keycloak takes the change.

P25a: for a person who lost every passkey and recovery code, once an administrator has made
sure it is them: their passkeys, authenticator-app codes and recovery codes are removed and
their sessions end; at their next sign-in (password first) they add a new passkey.

P25a: "Try again" on a sign-in change Keycloak refused or could not take: the person's
failed changes are queued again, in their order.

patch.description:
Change a person's role or active state. Portal administrators only.

The whole change is ONE transaction opened here, not left to ATOMIC_REQUESTS: ninja turns a
refusal into a 4xx response without letting the exception reach Django, so the request
transaction would commit whatever ran before it. Without this, a role change could stick while
the deactivation sent with it was refused.

get.description: The person's signature, or `has_image: false` when they have none.

post.description: A PNG or JPEG chosen from the person's computer.
What the pad drew: the canvas as a PNG (`toBlob`).

get.description:
What the caller is asked to decide (Tasks › Approvals, 234): the interns' letters and
messages they may approve, and the questions put to them. Only subjects they may see.
What the caller submitted, newest first, with its decision.
Whether the caller may file or send this subject now, and if not, why.

A subject's reviews, newest first; or (P20h) the approvals on one request, for its page's
strip (233, 238): waiting since when, or sent back by whom with what note. Scoped by the
subject, or by the request, as everywhere.

post.description:
Approve (and send: an intern's message is queued exactly as Send queues it), send back with
a note, or answer a question. Who may decide is the service's (`review.may_approve`).
The intern who submitted it takes it back while it waits (233).

patch.description: Name a holiday already on the calendar (or clear its name). Administrators only.

post.description: Every signed-in tab sends one a minute; the answer is the list, so one call does both.

get.description: Administrators: the sent-data log, newest first.

A requester sees their own; admins, staff and staff attorneys see every open one
(`pending`) or everything; a limited-scope attorney or an intern sees their own too (P20h:
taking a suggestion up is staff's).

post.description: Take it up: a letter draft in the caller's name, opened at `/drafts/{draft_id}`.

The last step's button. Refused (422, with the reason) while an agreement in force is not
accepted or no signature is stored.

get.description: Every version of each agreement, newest first within a kind (administrators).

post.description:
Publish the next version of an agreement (administrators). Everyone it applies to is asked
to agree to it at their next sign-in.

Agree to this version, signed with the caller's stored signature. The client address and
the browser are recorded with it, and a PDF of what was signed is kept.

get.description:
The caller's signed agreements; anyone's, or everyone's for one version, for an
administrator.

The PDF of exactly what was signed: the person themself or an administrator; anyone else
is answered as if it did not exist.
Every active person, for the new-message picker and @mentions: names only.

Who's online inside the panel (DECISIONS 32, 33c): everyone else seen lately, online first.
Everyone is told where people are by destination only; an administrator is told the
request. A requester is told nobody, as P19a's list told them nobody.

While the socket is down the client asks this every few seconds, with the `now` of its last
answer (less a little, and it drops what it already has).

Every agency by name. One merged into another is left out unless asked for (P16). Each
row carries its open and total requests and its median time to a determination (163), over
the requests the caller may see only, so a request hidden from them moves no figure.

post.description:
What importing this file would do, row by row: new, matching an agency already here (by
name and jurisdiction, merged names included), or a problem. Writes nothing. `mapping` is a
JSON object of column to field (null: not imported); left out, the columns are matched by
their headers.

Import the file: every new row is added, a matching row is filled in only where the
agency is blank and only if `decisions` (JSON, row number to "update" or "skip") says so,
a row with a problem is left out. All in one transaction; one activity line; nothing is
deleted or overwritten.

patch.description:
Edit a contact: a field left out is left alone; each change is an audit line with `note`.
Making a contact the primary one clears the previous primary in the same transaction.

get.description:
The agency page: the agency, its requests (newest first) and its response record.

The requests go through the same scoping the docket uses and the response record is computed
over only the requests that survive it, so a request hidden from this viewer cannot move a
figure they are shown.

get.description:
P15c, "Export the registry" (043): the docket as the caller sees it, with the same filters.
`ids` exports exactly the rows selected on the Docket; an id the caller may not see is left
out like any other hidden row. P23b: as text with commas, JSON or a PDF summary (the same
fields as a plain table), narrowed to the requests made between `since` and `until` (the
caller's own dates, inclusive), and each export is an activity line. Registered before
`/requests/{request_id}` so the path is not read as an id.

The Docket's stat strip in one read, counted under the list's own visibility rule. "Today"
is the caller's civil date in their own time zone.

parameters.name: span

schema.description: How many calendar dates, ending today, to count. Default: the setting `records.docket_history_span`; at most 366.

parameters.description: How many calendar dates, ending today, to count. Default: the setting `records.docket_history_span`; at most 366.

get.description:
The two sparklines: for each date, how many requests the caller may see were open and how
many overdue at its end, rebuilt from the status ledger. Nothing is stored.

Each person's open requests as the caller may see them (the assign dialog's "4 open"), by
the person's id. Someone with none is absent.

P23b (069 "Export the record as PDF"): the request's header, items, deadlines, status
ledger and its thread's messages, as one PDF in the reader's own time zone, through the
portal's PDF path. Whoever may see the request may export it; each export is an activity
line.

post.description:
P23b (083): the deadlines filing at `filed_at` would open, computed by the same rules
service filing uses, writing nothing. Read only, so open to whoever may see the request.
Say who is working this request; `user_id: null` unassigns.
New wording for some items, with the reason. Replying to the agency is not part of this.

"Add a document": a scan, a portal download or an email file becomes one source, its
attachments and one inbound event on this request. Multipart: the fields of `DocumentIn` and any
number of `files`. File names are sanitised; size and count limits are settings (422 past
them). Saying what the document MEANS is POST /events/{id}/classify afterwards.

get.description:
Every file on this request, oldest first: the Files tab, and the files under each message
in Correspondence (each carries its `source_id`).
The notes written on this request's messages. With its `note` events, the Notes tab.

post.description:
`status=production_received` here is refused by the chokepoint -- reason is always
'event', never 'manual_override', so `_append_status_change` raises NotAllowed (403).
Non-negotiable #4's one legal door is POST /requests/{id}/status.

get.description:
Both tables' own `sort_order` column exists precisely for display order, and every sibling
list endpoint in this API orders explicitly -- so this one does too, instead of relying on the
models' `Meta.ordering` to keep doing it invisibly.

parameters.name: kind

schema.description: A classification.
schema.title: Kind

parameters.description: A classification.

get.description:
What "Record as..." will do to this event's request, before anything is written. Driven by
the same table as the write, so it shows what the write then does. Valid kinds are GET
/definitions' `classifications`.

post.description:
Record an inbound event as one of the classifications, in one transaction.

"Production - complete" is the one row that cannot ride the event: it is written as a manual
override, which needs a note. The service is atomic, so a refusal at any step leaves the
request exactly as it was.

An unknown `deadline_type` trips the foreign key to deadline_definitions and surfaces as
IntegrityError, mapped to 422 by the API's global handler (HANDOFF convention 9).

`supersedes` replaces an EXISTING deadline's date with this new one, which is exactly what
POST /deadlines/{id}/supersede does, so it needs the same administrator. Guarding that door
and leaving this one open would make the rule a formality.

`payload.supersedes`, if the client sent one, is ignored -- the path id is what this new
deadline supersedes. There is no service door that marks an EXISTING deadline superseded by
another existing one; opening a new deadline with `supersedes=<old id>` is the only path.

One of the two doors that move an existing deadline's date, so an administrator's.

The "Resolve due date" dialog. The deadline in the path is the date that STANDS; the body
names the competing one, which becomes superseded by it. Returns the deadline that stands.
Put a message in front of a person and say why (`reason`: GET /definitions' flag_reasons).

Say who is dealing with a message; `user_id: null` unassigns. Not `/assign`, which attaches
the message to a request.
Take a message back out of "reviewed". Who had reviewed it stays in the audit log.
"Mark handled without attaching". Refused (409) while the message has a non-voided event.
A mistaken note is voided, never deleted.

"Mark files as records": exactly the named attachments are the records. Returns every file
of the message as it now stands.

get.description: The untouched original of a message (the stored JSON or .eml), as a download.

The requests a message may also be about: ones its text names by their address or by the
agency's own reference number, or the several it was addressed to. Worked out now, from the
stored original, and limited to requests the caller may see; nothing about a candidate is
stored on the message.

A message as a person reads it: who it is from and to, its subject, its date and its text,
read now from the stored original. This is the only way to read mail that is attached to no
request yet (an attached message's text is also on its event). `readable` is false for a
source that is not mail, or whose original cannot be read; download the original instead.

`open` is the original switch (true: open tasks, false: all of them) and is kept so nothing

`request_id` naming a request that does not exist trips `tasks.request_id`'s FK and
surfaces as django.db.IntegrityError, not a ServiceError -- caught by the API's global
IntegrityError -> 422 handler (see records/api/__init__.py).

patch.description:
Edit a task's due date or description. A field left out is left alone; `due_at: null`
clears the date. Every change is an audit line carrying `note`.

post.description: Hand a task to a person; `user_id: null` unassigns.
Undo a completion. Who had completed it is kept in the audit log.

get.description:
What changed on a task and who changed it (177, 178): its audit lines, oldest first. A
task is seen by whoever sees its request, so its history is too.

A task's notes, oldest first, voided ones included (P23b, 177). Seen by whoever sees the
task's request.

post.description: Write a note on a task ("Write a note…", 177). Never edited afterwards; void it instead.

Strike a note through with a reason. The note is addressed under its task, so the task's
request decides who may, and a note of another task is not found.

An invalid `status` trips fees.status's CHECK constraint and surfaces as
django.db.IntegrityError -- caught by the API's global handler (see records/api/__init__.py).

One bucket of the Inbox, newest first unless `sort` says otherwise, with the count of
every bucket for the navigation. `since` and `until` narrow it to when it arrived, in the

One message as an Inbox row, with the buckets it is in now (P23b). Seen by whoever may
see the message; where it landed on a request the caller may not see is left off the row,
exactly as on the list.
Overdue, due soon, assigned to you, and the flagged mail, all computed on the spot.

get.description:
Every deadline falling due from `start` to `end`: the active ones, and the satisfied,
waived and missed ones with their `status` so a finished one can be struck. Each
jurisdiction calendar's weekend and holidays in that range, with the names an administrator
typed. There is no calendar table.

The rules and calendars as they stand. Written through /core/rules (P18b), by an
administrator, each rule under its citation.

Who this request has been given to, oldest first: on a privileged request the people who
see it besides administrators and its requester of record; on any request, the limited-scope
attorneys and interns it was given to (and anyone else an administrator listed).

post.description:
Give this request to someone on the team. Administrators only (403 for anyone else); 409
if the person already has it; 422 for a requester or someone deactivated.

End one person's access. Administrators only. 409 when they are the last person on a
privileged request's list who can still open it.

get.description:
Administrators only: the privileged requests the caller is NOT on the list of, by tracking
number and nothing else. It opens none of them. To open one, the administrator adds themselves
with POST /requests/{id}/access, which leaves a row saying they did.

post.description:
The one door a staff member reaches on a privileged request they cannot see: asking for
it. Not `require_request_scope`, on purpose. A request that does not exist is a 404 as
elsewhere for staff; one the caller already sees is refused by the service (409).

get.description: Every ask on this request, for an administrator (who decides them).
Every open ask, for an administrator; empty for anyone else on staff.

The caller's own asks and their answers. Names the tracking numbers they asked about,
which they already had from the page that refused them.

post.description:
Record a production review. Every item of the request gets a disposition; the files named
become records tied to the request and, where given, an item. Every item produced is the
person declaring the request fully produced; anything else is a partial production.

get.description: What a review of this production starts from. Reads only; the dialog is built from it.

schema.description: By when received.
schema.title: Order

parameters.description: By when received.

get.description:
Every produced file across the requests the caller may see, newest first (or oldest
first: the Records screen's Date order, 039).

schema.description: Attachment ids, comma-separated.
schema.title: Ids

parameters.description: Attachment ids, comma-separated.

get.description:
"Download as a set": the named files, as one zip. Every file named must be one the caller
may see (the same refusal as its own download), so a set never carries a file out that a
listing would have left out.

Live links in either direction. The other end is named even when the caller may not open
it: a link is a fact about this request, and the tracking number is already what the
"You don't have access" page shows.

post.description:
The letter went out some way other than the portal's mail. Not an intern's to say: their
letters leave only through approval (P20h).
P19h: a footnote of the block's own.
Retirement rather than deletion, and the only option once anything has been filed from it.

The editor's Save: record the template as it stands, with who saved it and what changed.
Editing writes no history; this does. Saving a template that has not changed since its newest
revision returns that revision and writes nothing.

P23b: `refile_reason` (097) is written as a note on the request the draft is started from,
in the same transaction, so "why it was filed again" stays on the first request's record.

delete.description:
Refused with a 409 once anything has been filed from it -- the schema's trigger, translated
into a sentence by the service layer rather than echoed as a constraint name.

get.description:
The draft a reserved request was made from (the request page's "Review & file", 076): the
newest letter that reserved it. 404 when the request was not made from a draft; the privileged
refusal when the draft is one this person may not open (a privileged draft is its creator's).
Exactly what filing would send, rendered through the same code path.

post.description:
Fan the draft out. Each recipient files in its own transaction, so one malformed row does
not roll back the others; a recipient that failed comes back in `outcomes` with its reason.

get.description:
"Preview as": the draft as it would read for an agency that is not a recipient yet, by the
channel given or else the agency's own filing method.

post.description:
Reserve this recipient's tracking number and alias and freeze its letter, without sending
anything. 422, naming them, while any blank in the letter is unresolved; 409 if it is already
reserved or is not pending.

Mark this one letter as sent, reserving it first if it has not been. The same filing as
POST /api/records/requests/{id}/file on its request; 409 if the letter is already out.

Decide not to send this letter. If it was already reserved this withdraws its request,
which needs `note`.

put.description:
The editor's save: the pieces and citations it holds replace the draft's; the plain text
of every piece is derived from its document here.

get.description:
The page as the screen shows it, for one agency's values or with the placeholders
standing.
Whether letters are written in the drafting tool now, and where its pages are.

post.description:
The drafting tool's webhooks (SCLU.md 9.3): verified over the exact bytes received (HMAC
v1, constant time, five minutes either way), recorded once by event id, then applied. A
delivery seen before is acknowledged and changes nothing (the fork retries with the same id).

What the Templates frame said about a template it created or changed (`sclu-templates/1`
"template"): the portal's row for it, so stage 1 offers it. Staff, as the library is.

Make the agency letters the drafting tool has not made yet (a reserve whose merge failed):
every reserved recipient of this draft still to go out and without one.

get.description:
One agency's merge values, for stage 2's "Preview as" before its letter exists: its
recipient's when it is one (with its contact and overrides), else the agency's own.

The letter from the drafting tool as the person asking: an agency's (`recipient_id`), else
the master. The same bytes for a version every time (SCLU.md 9.2).

The request's letter in the drafting tool, for its Files tab: which version, when it last
changed, its open review comments and its latest citation check, from the webhooks received.
Empty for a request not written there. The team's (a requester cannot use the drafting
tool, QUESTIONS 33).

get.description:
`since` and `until` (P23b, the Inbox's "Any time", 154) are the person's own dates, both
inclusive: a message counts from when it was sent, a draft from when it last changed.

post.description:
The follow-up the Docket's dialog (034) opens with, rendered here from the settings
templates the automatic follow-up uses. Read only: it creates nothing. Who may ask is who
may read the request.
A draft reply (or forward) to a message, prefilled from it, on its request.

Send is pressed: the message waits its undo window, then the worker sends it. An intern's
message is refused (403) unless it was approved and has not changed since: theirs go out
through approval (P20h; `send.queue` checks).

Stage 4, an email agency: the cover message is sent from the request's alias with the
letter attached, and the recipient's request is filed when the provider accepts it. Not an
intern's door (403, before anything is written): theirs is POST /mail/recipients/{id}/submit,
and an approver's "Approve and send" queues it as this does.

An intern's "Submit for approval" (232): the letter to this agency, with its cover message
when it goes by email, waits for an approver; the request becomes waiting for approval (233).
Anyone else gets 403: their stage 4 sends or files.
After a bounce, a person marks the agency contact's address as wrong.

EndSessionOut.description:
Keycloak's end-session endpoint and the fields to post to it (RP-initiated logout; posted,
so the ID token stays out of addresses).
EndSessionOut.title: EndSessionOut

SecondStepsOut.description:
Which second steps a person may set up (P25c): a passkey always; an authenticator app while
an administrator allows them (Settings → System → Sign-in).
SecondStepsOut.title: SecondStepsOut

UserPatch.description: Every field optional; what is left out is left alone.
UserPatch.title: UserPatch

DraftingToolOut.description:
P21c: the drafting tool's seam, for Settings → System. Whether the switch is on and the
tool is in use (the switch, both addresses and both secrets), each address in force and the
server's default under it, and whether each secret is set: never a secret's value. The address
the fork's webhooks are to be sent to, and when the last one arrived. (P25b: the tool signs in
through Keycloak; the end-sessions secret is gone.)
DraftingToolOut.title: DraftingToolOut

The newest registry export (P23b; 199 "Last registry export · Dana Nolan · CSV"): who,
the format, when, how many requests and the range. No request is named.

P25a: the sign-in, Keycloak's. Where it is (the realm's public address), where an
administrator opens its own console, whether the server holds both client secrets (never the
secrets), and the changes still owed to it (`KeycloakChange`: pending, failed).
SignInOut.title: SignInOut

HolidayNameIn.title: HolidayNameIn

ChatPartOut.description:
One piece of a message as the reader may see it. `kind` is text | mention | request | page
| url. A request the reader may not see is `{kind: request, text: "a request"}` and nothing
else: no id, no title, no link.
ChatPartOut.title: ChatPartOut

ChatSeenOut.description: One person in who's online, as the reader may be told it (DECISIONS 33c).
ChatSeenOut.title: ChatSeenOut

AgencyRowOut.description:
A row of the Agencies list (163): the agency and two figures over the requests the caller
may see, the ones of the agencies merged into it included. `open_requests` counts those not
closed, denied or withdrawn; `requests_total` every one (the "Most requests" order); the
median is calendar dates from filing to the first determination, as Reports count it, over
every year.
AgencyRowOut.title: AgencyRowOut

ClosuresIn.description: One closure per agency named. The citation is the person's; the portal fills nothing.
ClosuresIn.title: ClosuresIn

AgencyImportRowOut.description: One row of an uploaded agency list as the import would treat it (168).
AgencyImportRowOut.title: AgencyImportRowOut

ContactPatchIn.description:
Edit a contact (171). A field left out is left alone; every change is an audit line
carrying `note`.
ContactPatchIn.title: ContactPatchIn

ResponseRecordOut.description:
Computed from events and deadlines on every call; stored nowhere. The date-based figures
are null for an agency whose law has no calendar mapped.
ResponseRecordOut.title: ResponseRecordOut

DocketSummaryOut.description:
The stat strip (025), counted under the same visibility rule as the list. The three status
lists are what the matching boxes count, so the screen filters the list by exactly them.
DocketSummaryOut.title: DocketSummaryOut

PlannedDeadlineOut.description:
A deadline filing would open (083 "Determination due Sep 18 · …"): from the rules, with
the legal basis as the rule states it.
PlannedDeadlineOut.title: PlannedDeadlineOut

ProvisionGapOut.description: An item's provision with no rule in force: filing opens an "enter rules" task for it.
ProvisionGapOut.title: ProvisionGapOut

FilingPreviewIn.description:
What filing would be told (083), to ask what it would open before filing: the moment,
and the provisions as `FileRequestIn` takes them.
FilingPreviewIn.title: FilingPreviewIn

AssignRequestIn.description:
Assigning a request (036). `notify` is "Tell them by email": the new assignee is always
told in the portal, and by email too only when this is true and their own preference for
assignments allows it. Left out, it is false.
AssignRequestIn.title: AssignRequestIn

DocumentIn.description: The form fields of POST /requests/{id}/documents; the files travel beside them.
DocumentIn.title: DocumentIn

ClassificationKindOut.description:
One item of the "Record as..." / "Log a response" menu, from the table that also drives the
preview and the write.
ClassificationKindOut.title: ClassificationKindOut

ClassifyPreviewOut.description:
What recording this event as this kind will do. `deadlines` are the request's active ones as
they stand; classifying changes none of them.
ClassifyPreviewOut.title: ClassifyPreviewOut

ResolveDeadlineIn.description: The deadline in the path is the one that STANDS; this names the one that is dropped.
ResolveDeadlineIn.title: ResolveDeadlineIn

ResolveSourceIn.description: The note is required for `other` and optional otherwise.
ResolveSourceIn.title: ResolveSourceIn

SourceRecordsIn.description: Exactly these attachments of the message are the records; one not named stops being one.
SourceRecordsIn.title: SourceRecordsIn

CandidateOut.description: A request a flagged message may also be about.
CandidateOut.title: CandidateOut

MessageOut.description: A stored message, read for a person. Plain text only; markup is never passed through.
MessageOut.title: MessageOut

TaskPatchIn.description: A field left out is left alone; `due_at: null` clears the date.
TaskPatchIn.title: TaskPatchIn

TaskHistoryOut.description:
One change to a task, from the audit log (177, 178): who, which field, from what to what,
and the note they gave. Creation and completion are on the task itself.
TaskHistoryOut.title: TaskHistoryOut

TaskNoteOut.description:
A note on a task (177 "Write a note…"). A voided note is still listed, with who voided it,
when and why.
TaskNoteOut.title: TaskNoteOut

FeePatchIn.description:
PATCH: a field left out is left alone, and only an explicit null clears it. `status` and
`note` are required.
FeePatchIn.title: FeePatchIn

InboxCountsOut.description: Messages in each bucket. Not narrowed by the search or the filters.
InboxCountsOut.title: InboxCountsOut

InboxEventOut.description: Where a message landed: one non-voided event of it, with its request and agency.
InboxEventOut.title: InboxEventOut

InboxItemOut.description:
One message as an Inbox row (P23b), read by its id, with the buckets it is in now: a
message opened by its address beyond the loaded page, or one that left the list it was
opened from (140), or the full-page message (107 "Open full page").
InboxItemOut.title: InboxItemOut

DeadlineRowOut.description:
A deadline with the request it belongs to and how far off it is. Home lists active ones;
the Calendar also lists satisfied, waived and missed ones, so `status` says which.

MissingRuleOut.description: An open enter_deadline_rules task: a provision a request names that no rule covers.
MissingRuleOut.title: MissingRuleOut

AccessOut.description: One person's access to one privileged request. `revoked_at` is null while it is in force.
AccessOut.title: AccessOut

AccessIn.description: Share a privileged request with `user_id`, a member of staff. `note` says why.
AccessIn.title: AccessIn

UnlistedOut.description: A privileged request the caller cannot see: enough to ask for it or add oneself, no more.
UnlistedOut.title: UnlistedOut

ReviewSheetOut.description:
What a review of this event starts from: the event's files, every item with the
disposition that stands for it today, and what a review with every item produced means.
ReviewSheetOut.title: ReviewSheetOut

ChallengeIn.description:
Open a challenge and, unless `with_letter` is false, start its letter as a mail draft on
the request, addressed to the agency, for the person to write.
ChallengeIn.title: ChallengeIn

SaveTemplateIn.description: The editor's Save. `summary` is the line on what changed.
SaveTemplateIn.title: SaveTemplateIn

TemplateBlocksIn.description:
The shared blocks a template pulls in. Blocks and items share one `sort_order` sequence,
so `sort_orders` (one per block, same order) places each block among the items: before the
item with that number, or after them all. Left out, the blocks take 0, 1, 2... as given.
TemplateBlocksIn.title: TemplateBlocksIn

LetterSaveIn.description: What the editor holds. A list given replaces the rows of that kind; one left out is kept.
LetterSaveIn.title: LetterSaveIn

RequestDraftOut.description:
The draft a reserved request was made from, and the letter (recipient) that reserved it:
where the request page's "Review & file" (076) goes.
RequestDraftOut.title: RequestDraftOut

FileRecipientIn.description: Mark one letter as sent. `filed_at` defaults to now, `channel` to the recipient's own.
FileRecipientIn.title: FileRecipientIn

SkipIn.description: `note` is required once the recipient is reserved: skipping then withdraws its request.
SkipIn.title: SkipIn

ForkStatusOut.description:
Whether letters are written in the drafting tool now, and where its pages are (for the
frames and their message origin checks). The addresses only while it is in use.
ForkStatusOut.title: ForkStatusOut

ForkTemplateIn.description: `sclu-templates/1`'s "template" message, as the Templates frame posted it.
ForkTemplateIn.title: ForkTemplateIn

ForkValuesOut.description:
One agency's merge values, for stage 2's "Preview as" before its letter exists
(`sclu-letter/1` "preview").
ForkValuesOut.title: ForkValuesOut

ForkLetterOut.description: A request's letter in the drafting tool, for its Files tab.
ForkLetterOut.title: ForkLetterOut

SendingOut.description:
Whether messages really go out (`MAIL_SEND_ENABLED`); off means the provider's test
token, which accepts and discards.
SendingOut.title: SendingOut

FollowupDraftOut.description:
A follow-up filled from the organisation's templates, for a person to change and send.
Nothing is saved by asking for it.
FollowupDraftOut.title: FollowupDraftOut

SendAndFileIn.description:
Stage 4 of New request, for an email agency: the cover message and who gets it. The
letter is attached as a PDF; the request is filed when the provider accepts the message.

ApprovalRef.description: What submitting a letter for approval made: the review, and the request it waits on.
ApprovalRef.title: ApprovalRef

SubmitLetterIn.description:
Stage 4 for an intern (232): the cover message as `SendAndFileIn` (an email agency's; left
empty for a web form or post) and a note for the approver.
